_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as evidence of a real, long-running Danish gaming-decoration community; do not use verbatim as a page title without more evidence of current (not just 2009-era) usage.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in formal/editorial copy — it's a community group name, not a general term.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use in FAQ/technical-explainer contexts (e.g. 'how to type special characters in Windows'); use 'fede tegn' instead for gaming/casual/decoration contexts — the two terms serve different registers, don't conflate them.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in a casual gaming-name-decoration headline — it reads as a technical support term, not a style term.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'skråskrift' for the cursive generator style; reserve 'løkkeskrift' for handwriting-practice/printable contexts; keep 'kursiv' strictly for italic.
phrases.good_example: Skriv dit navn i skråskrift og kopiér det til din bio.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not label the italic style 'skråskrift', and do not label the cursive style 'kursiv'.

phrases.english_concept: English term dominance — 'font generator' left untranslated in Danish
phrases.usage_guidance: Treat this as a signal to *test*, not a licence to write English headings. If a da/ page is built, the defensible shape is a Danish H1 using 'skrifttypegenerator' with the English 'font generator' appearing naturally once in the intro or an FAQ — not a bilingual keyword-stuffed title. Crucially, this finding bears on whether a localized da/ page is worth building at all; it should be settled with query-level data before anyone commits.
phrases.good_example: Skrifttypegenerator (font generator) — skriv, vælg en stil, og kopiér.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not put both the English and Danish forms in one title as near-synonyms. Do not conclude from this alone that Danish pages are unnecessary.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'gamer-navn' in gaming-name sections and 'brugernavn' only for the account field. Danish orthography prefers the hyphenated compound 'gamer-navn' over the space-separated 'gamer navn' seen in casual writing.
phrases.good_example: Et gamer-navn er mere end bare et brugernavn — det er din identitet i spillet.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'gamer-navn' for a non-gaming social profile, or as a synonym for the login field.

phrases.english_concept: copy and paste (as an everyday action)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'Kopiér' alone as a button label and the full phrase in instructions. Pick one accent convention per page and keep it consistent.
phrases.good_example: Kopiér den konverterede tekst, og indsæt den, hvor du vil.
phrases.avoid_when: Never render 'paste' as 'sæt ind' split incorrectly, or as a paste cognate.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'fed skrift'/'fed tekst' as the bold style label. For blackletter, lead with 'gammel engelsk tekst' (recognised) and mention 'gotisk skrift'/'fraktur' once as the proper name — do not lead with the trade term.
phrases.good_example: Fed skrift til din bio — vælg stilen og kopiér.
phrases.avoid_when: Careful with register: 'fed' also means 'awesome' in Danish slang (cf. DA-001 'fede tegn'). In a style list the typographic sense is unambiguous, but avoid 'fed' in prose where the slang reading could take over.

phrases.english_concept: cool/awesome text -- modern slang sense confirmed via Denmark's own standard dictionary
phrases.usage_guidance: Already in correct use on da/index.html and by real competitors.
phrases.avoid_when: formal/technical contexts -- 'sej' in its older dictionary senses means 'tough/chewy/pliable', not 'cool'; only the modern slang sense fits this product

phrases.english_concept: the specific job-to-be-done query: converting one's own name into runic script, used verbatim by Denmark's National Museum
phrases.usage_guidance: H1/meta for a rune-name feature or explainer.

phrases.english_concept: popular nickname for the Jelling Stone -- a UNESCO-anchored cultural hook unique to Denmark for any future rune-heritage content
phrases.usage_guidance: Editorial hook for hero copy/intro prose on any future rune-heritage content -- NOT a search-volume keyword itself.
phrases.avoid_when: do not use in a title/meta as if it were a search term -- it's an evocative editorial phrase, not a query people type

phrases.native_phrase: Harald Blåtand / Bluetooth-runer (Hagall ᚼ + Bjarkan ᛒ)
phrases.english_concept: the real trivia that the Bluetooth tech logo is a bind-rune of Danish King Harald Bluetooth's initials in Younger Futhark
phrases.usage_guidance: Color/hook for a rune-heritage intro, or an FAQ 'did you know' item -- globally relatable trivia, but Denmark-specific ownership of the story.

phrases.english_concept: youth-slang framing for wanting fancy/decorated text ('look a little extra')
phrases.content_surface: marketing copy / hero tagline / social captions
phrases.usage_guidance: Good as a tone reference for DK marketing copy — captures the self-aware, slightly playful register Danish users reach for, better than a literal 'fancy text' translation.
